document.title: Commvault REST API Reference (Job Operations, Authentication Operations)

supplementary_document.title: Commvault REST API Reference (official PDF, complete)
supplementary_document.note: Supplied directly by the customer as a local file, not a public URL. Used on 2026-08-31 to re-verify ATLAS-IMP-267/269 against the complete documented parameter tables (rather than only the individual api.commvault.com reference pages cited below), which surfaced and corrected three real discrepancies (ATLAS-IMP-270: an incomplete job-status vocabulary, an over-scoped required IsDeletedClient/osInfo.Type on the Client list read, and an over-scoped required numberOfCopies on the StoragePolicy list read) and confirmed a real GET-based recovery-point read path (ATLAS-IMP-271: GET Subclient + GET Subclient/{id}/Browse), closing a gap ATLAS-IMP-269 had mistakenly called unresolvable.

capability_sources.note: Endpoint path, query parameters (jobFilter, jobCategory, completedJobLookupTime), and the complete response field set were confirmed directly from the official api.commvault.com machine-generated reference page, which shows a literal, complete example JSON response: {"totalRecordsWithoutPaging": N, "jobs": [{"jobSummary": {"jobId", "status", "jobType", "percentComplete", "jobStartTime", "subclientName", "destClientName", "subclient": {"clientName", ...}, ...}}]}. The complete 19-value status vocabulary (Running, Waiting, Pending, Suspend, Suspended, Kill Pending, Interrupt Pending, Interrupted, Queued, Running (cannot be verified), Abnormal Terminated, Cleanup, Completed, Completed w/ one or more errors, Completed w/ one or more warnings, Committed, Failed, Failed to Start, Killed) is confirmed via the official PDF reference's own "Valid values are" table for jobSummary.status (see supplementary_document); any value outside this set still maps to an honest UNKNOWN rather than being guessed.

Endpoint path and clientId/clientName/hostName were confirmed directly from the official api.commvault.com machine-generated reference page. The official PDF reference's own response-parameter table for this exact list endpoint (as opposed to the single-client GET Client/{clientId} endpoint, whose table is longer) documents only clientEntity.{clientId, clientName, hostName, displayName, clientGUID} and clientProps.enableAccessControl -- confirmed further by a literal example list response whose clientProps element carries only enableAccessControl. Neither clientProps.IsDeletedClient nor any osInfo.Type field is confirmed present on this list read, so both are read defensively and modeled as optional; a client is only flagged as a protection-coverage finding on a confirmed IsDeletedClient == true.

The full path (with the V2 prefix) was confirmed via a separate community/documentation source describing the same GET/PUT/DELETE StoragePolicy endpoint family. The official PDF reference's own response-parameter table for this exact list endpoint documents only storagePolicyName/storagePolicyId (element: policies), and its literal example response (<policies numberOfStreams="1"><storagePolicy storagePolicyId="2" storagePolicyName="SP1"/>...) confirms numberOfStreams is present but numberOfCopies is not. numberOfCopies -- the one field this connector treats as a real redundancy signal (a policy with zero copies retains no backup data) -- is therefore not read from this list endpoint; see the separate GET .../StoragePolicy/{id}?propertyLevel=10 source below.

The "GET Storage Policy Details" operation and its propertyLevel parameter (1 = ID and name only, 10 = complete information) are confirmed in the official PDF reference (see supplementary_document); its literal propertyLevel=10 example response (<policies ... numberOfStreams="50" ... numberOfCopies="5" ...>) is where numberOfCopies is actually confirmed present. Read as a bounded, per-policy enrichment call (first 25 policies) after the list read, mirroring the vCenter host-to-cluster membership precedent from ATLAS-IMP-268; a policy whose Details read fails is left with number_of_copies=None rather than failing the whole overview.

"GET Subclient" is confirmed in the official PDF reference (see supplementary_document), including a literal example XML response for clientId=2/clientName=client001 showing two subclients, each a subClientEntity.{subclientId, subclientName, applicationId, appName, backupsetId, backupsetName, clientId, clientName, instanceId, instanceName}. This connector reads subclientId, subclientName, clientId, and appName -- the confirmed prerequisite identifiers for the per-subclient Browse read below (Commvault's Browse operation targets a subclient, not a client directly).

"GET Subclient Browse" (root-level browse, path=%5C) is confirmed in the official PDF reference (see supplementary_document) with a literal, complete example response: databrowse_BrowseResponseList -> browseResponses[] (respType, workerId) -> browseResult (queryId) -> dataResultSet (name, path, displayPath, modificationTime, displayName, size) -> advancedData (archiveGroupId, referenceTime, archiveFileId, backupJobId, backupTime, ...). Two real, documented collapsing ambiguities are handled defensively rather than assumed: (1) browseResponses commonly holds a second, sibling entry carrying only an aggrResultSet count (no items) alongside the entry with real dataResultSet items -- both entries are examined, and only dataResultSet items are kept; (2) dataResultSet may be a single object or a list depending on item count. Read as a bounded sample only (first 3 clients x first 3 subclients x first 5 items each, ATLAS-IMP-271), not an exhaustive recovery-point catalog.

authentication_source.note: Confirmed directly from Commvault's own official documentation page, which shows the exact endpoint (`POST $[webservice]/Login`), request body fields (username, password [Base64 UTF-8 encoded], domain, commserver, timeout), and the response token field (`"token": "QSDK ..."`). A second independent official source (api.commvault.com's AuthenticationOperations/login page) corroborated the `Authtoken` header requirement for subsequent requests -- a genuine, confirmed difference from every other connector built for this project, which all use either a vendor-specific token header (X-Auth-Token, vmware-api-session-id) or Authorization: Bearer/Basic, never a header literally named Authtoken. Token validity: 30 minutes of inactivity by default. Logout (`POST webservice/Logout` with the same Authtoken header, no body) was confirmed the same way. This connector follows the established login -> read -> logout bounded-cycle pattern used for both Huawei connectors and vCenter, never caching a live session.

self_test_source.note: No confirmed dedicated version/compatibility endpoint independent of the job-status read was found; the self-test reuses a narrow, one-hour-lookback job-status read itself, the same pattern used for every prior connector's probe.

unconfirmed_gaps: No confirmed field connects a Commvault-protected client or storage policy to entities from any other connector in this project, so no cross-vendor graph relationship (e.g. BACKED_BY) is asserted.

The recovery-point catalog (ATLAS-IMP-271) is a small, bounded sample -- the first 3 clients' first 3 subclients' first 5 root-level browse items each -- not an exhaustive catalog of all backed-up data. Widening this would require deliberate, explicit budget increases, not a redesign.

A real but different question -- mapping which storage policy is assigned to a specific subclient -- has no confirmed bulk REST endpoint (per a real community thread); only the storage-policy list itself (this connector's scope) and Commvault's own admin console/per-subclient properties API cover that.
